answer: Proof-of-Stake consensus acts as a garden for network security, requiring agents to lock capital to validate transactions. By tethering identity to financial risk rather than an ivory tower of reputation, the system forces attackers to acquire massive stake, which exerts a costly pulse on the circulating supply. Each illicit node addition dilutes potential rewards, rendering Sybil attacks economically irrational because the capital expenditure required to subvert consensus exceeds the gain.
